speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the Ministry has data on the number of families that will be affected when childcare centres are no longer mandated to operate on Saturdays from 1 January 2025; and (b) whether companies operating on shift hours especially on weekends have been engaged on this change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: When announcing these changes in July 2023, we recognised that sufficient lead time was necessary to minimise the impact to families which may be affected ahead of the implementation of the changes in January 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Kindly allow me to share how we started this journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In October 2022, Minister Masagos, the Minister for Social and Family Development, had announced that ECDA would engage parents, operators and educators to co-develop ways to improve working conditions, with outcomes to be shared by mid-2023.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A key idea then, which resonated strongly, was the review of the requirement of provision of Saturday childcare services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: From November 2022 to January 2023, ECDA carried out public consultations with the stakeholders and analysis on the initiatives to improve working conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As Members can see, we had started this process early.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Families were informed early, so that they could make alternative caregiving arrangements or work out appropriate arrangements with their employers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, employees can request for flexible workplace arrangements with employers, and the employers have to properly consider and assess, as set out in the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Workplace Arrangement Requests.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Several small and medium enterprises (SMEs) owners who operate on weekends, such as retail, food and beverage (F&B) and essential services business owners, have expressed concern on the lack of childcare support options on Saturdays.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Despite the much earlier announcement in 2023, they tell me that they are unaware of the changes and have not factored this into their scheduling plans.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would the Ministry be doing another round of engagements with employers before the changes take place in January 2025?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And would the Ministry also provide updates on alternatives on other affordable weekend childcare options?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I know that the Member has been a strong advocate for the retail, as well as the F&B industry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I take in her feedback and ECDA takes in this feedback seriously.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As we have shared, we started this journey very early.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ECDA had been sending out letters to the preschool operators to inform them that there is no need to provide Saturday childcare services if there is no requirement to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have also sent out letter templates to these preschool operators for them to send out to the parents of the children to inform them that we will be stopping the provision of the Saturday preschool services starting 1 January 2025.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Following from this initiative, we will also be further sharing with the families that they can consider tapping on paid, as well as community-based options, such as the home-based childminding programme by Daughters of Tomorrow as well as other services, such as playgroup and enrichment classes, which are conducted at the community clubs and centres on Saturday mornings.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My focus is more on the early childhood educators.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But I note that with the removal of Saturday services, work that the preschool teachers used to do on Saturdays would now need to be done on the weekdays.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I understand that this would include lesson preparation, administrative work, classroom set-up and even attending training.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, beyond the physical working hours, I am quite concerned about the hours that our early childhood educators spend outside of these official working hours, in particular, attending to parents' queries.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is a common issue that teachers face.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I note that the Minister for Education had recently stated that the Ministry of Education teachers are not required to respond to work-related messages after school hours.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I would, therefore, like to ask if ECDA could provide early childhood educators with a similar right to disconnect, so that they can have protected rest time outside of their work hours.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is a continuous work-in-progress and I think we are totally on the same page, aligned in our common interests to make sure that we improve the working conditions of our early childhood educators.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I take the Member's point on the right to disconnect and I think this is something that the Member has been championing across various sectors and industries for our workers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I will share that with ECDA and I thank the Member very much for his feedback.
